subject: Biology
description: Covers Vitamins A, C, D, B12, and Protein deficiency (Kwashiorkor).

questions.stem: Night blindness and xerophthalmia (dryness of the eye) are primarily caused by the deficiency of:

options.option_text: Vitamin A (Retinol)
Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
Vitamin D (Calciferol)
Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Vitamin A is essential for the formation of rhodopsin, a light-sensitive pigment in the retina necessary for low-light vision. Deficiency first leads to night blindness (nyctalopia) and, if severe, progresses to xerophthalmia, where the cornea becomes dry, thick, and opaque, eventually leading to irreversible blindness. 
DECOY BUSTING: Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy (bleeding gums). Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets (soft bones in children). Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi (nerve and heart issues).
EXAM INSIGHT: In developing countries, Vitamin A deficiency is a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness. The Indian government runs a massive prophylaxis program administering high-dose Vitamin A drops to children under 5. Golden Rice (genetically modified) was specifically designed to produce beta-carotene (a precursor to Vitamin A) to combat this deficiency.

questions.stem: Kwashiorkor, a form of severe malnutrition characterized by a swollen belly (edema), is primarily caused by a diet severely deficient in:

options.option_text: Protein
Carbohydrates
Iron
Fats

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kwashiorkor is a protein-deficiency disease. It typically affects young children in impoverished regions, often occurring when a baby is weaned off high-protein breast milk onto a diet of starchy, low-protein gruel (like yam or cassava). The lack of dietary protein means the blood lacks albumin. Albumin is necessary to maintain osmotic pressure; without it, fluid leaks from the blood vessels into the abdominal cavity, causing the characteristic swollen, protruding belly (edema).
DECOY BUSTING: A severe deficiency in BOTH calories (carbohydrates) and protein causes Marasmus, which presents differently: severe wasting, emaciation, and looking like "skin and bones," without the swollen belly. 
EXAM INSIGHT: Distinguishing between Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency, edema) and Marasmus (overall calorie/protein deficiency, wasting) is a classic biology question in competitive exams.

questions.stem: Which vitamin is synthesized by the human body upon exposure to sunlight, and its deficiency leads to Osteomalacia in adults?

options.option_text: Vitamin D
Vitamin E
Vitamin K
Vitamin B12

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Vitamin D (Calciferol) is uniquely synthesized in the skin from cholesterol when exposed to Ultraviolet B (UVB) rays from the sun. It is crucial for the intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus. A deficiency in children causes Rickets (bowed legs, soft bones). In adults, the equivalent condition is Osteomalacia (softening of bones), leading to bone pain and muscle weakness.
DECOY BUSTING: Vitamin E is an antioxidant. Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting. Vitamin B12 (found only in animal products) is vital for nerve function and red blood cell production; its deficiency causes pernicious anemia.
EXAM INSIGHT: Despite abundant sunshine, Vitamin D deficiency is a hidden epidemic in India due to indoor lifestyles, darker skin pigmentation (melanin acts as a natural sunblock, requiring more sun exposure to make Vitamin D), and air pollution blocking UVB rays.

questions.stem: A patient presents with swollen, bleeding gums, delayed wound healing, and extreme fatigue. Historically, this disease was common among sailors on long voyages. Which nutrient is deficient?

options.option_text: Vitamin C
Iron
Iodine
Vitamin A

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The symptoms describe Scurvy, caused by a severe lack of Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid). Vitamin C is an essential co-factor for the synthesis of collagen, the main structural protein in connective tissues, blood vessels, and skin. Without collagen, blood vessels become fragile (causing bleeding gums and skin bruises) and wounds fail to heal.
DECOY BUSTING: Iron deficiency causes anemia (fatigue, pale skin). Iodine deficiency causes goiter (enlarged thyroid). Vitamin A deficiency affects vision.
EXAM INSIGHT: Humans, unlike most other mammals, cannot synthesize Vitamin C internally due to a genetic mutation in our evolutionary past. We must obtain it from our diet (citrus fruits, peppers, amla). The British Navy famously started issuing lime juice to sailors to prevent scurvy, earning them the nickname "Limeys".

questions.stem: Pernicious anemia is a specific type of megaloblastic anemia caused by the body's inability to absorb which essential vitamin from the gastrointestinal tract?

options.option_text: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
Vitamin B9 (Folic Acid)
Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is essential for producing healthy red blood cells and maintaining the nervous system. However, to be absorbed in the small intestine, B12 MUST bind to a protein called 'Intrinsic Factor', which is produced by the parietal cells of the stomach. Pernicious anemia is an autoimmune condition where the body destroys its own parietal cells. Without Intrinsic Factor, B12 cannot be absorbed, leading to massive, immature red blood cells (megaloblastic anemia) and severe nerve damage.
DECOY BUSTING: While Folic Acid (B9) deficiency also causes megaloblastic anemia, "pernicious anemia" refers strictly to the autoimmune B12 absorption failure. Niacin (B3) deficiency causes Pellagra (diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia). 
EXAM INSIGHT: Because Vitamin B12 is found almost exclusively in animal products (meat, dairy, eggs), strict vegans are at a high risk of dietary B12 deficiency (though this is dietary deficiency, not true pernicious anemia).

questions.stem: Beriberi, characterized by peripheral neuropathy, muscle weakness, and — in its 'wet' form — cardiac enlargement and oedema, is caused by deficiency of which vitamin?

options.option_text: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) — vital for cellular energy production
Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — essential for carbohydrate metabolism
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine) — required for amino acid metabolism
Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) — needed for nerve myelin maintenance

questions.explanation: Thiamine (B1) is a co-factor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase; its deficiency impairs carbohydrate metabolism and causes beriberi. B12 is the most tempting wrong answer because it also causes neurological symptoms, but B12 deficiency leads to megaloblastic anaemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord — not the wet/dry forms of beriberi.

questions.stem: Pellagra — classically described by dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia, and (if untreated) death — results from insufficient intake of which vitamin, especially in populations subsisting mainly on maize?

options.option_text: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) — causes ariboflavinosis with glossitis
Vitamin B3 (Niacin) — required for NAD/NADP synthesis in cells
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine) — linked to sideroblastic anaemia onset
Vitamin B9 (Folic acid) — critical for DNA synthesis and repair

questions.explanation: Niacin (B3) is required for synthesis of NAD and NADP, the principal redox co-enzymes in energy metabolism. Maize contains niacin in a bound, biologically unavailable form unless treated with alkali (nixtamalization). Riboflavin (B2) is the most common wrong pick because its deficiency also involves skin and mucosal features, but it causes ariboflavinosis — not pellagra's classic '4 Ds'.

questions.stem: Which clinical sign specifically distinguishes zinc deficiency from iron deficiency, as it is a hallmark of zinc deficiency but does NOT typically occur in iron-deficiency anaemia?

options.option_text: Pallor, fatigue, and reduced haemoglobin concentration in blood
Ageusia (loss of taste) and impaired wound healing in adults
Koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails) and brittle hair texture
Angular stomatitis and magenta discolouration of the tongue

questions.explanation: Zinc is essential for taste receptor function and metalloproteinase enzymes involved in wound healing; ageusia and poor wound healing are hallmarks of zinc deficiency. Pallor, fatigue, and koilonychia (spoon nails) are characteristic of iron deficiency. Angular stomatitis with a magenta tongue points to riboflavin (B2) deficiency — a classic distractor since mucosal signs can overlap across deficiencies.

questions.stem: Populations in landlocked mountainous regions develop enlarged thyroid glands and progressive hypothyroidism because the local soil and water are depleted of which mineral?

options.option_text: Selenium — needed for deiodinase enzymes that activate T3 hormone
Iodine — structural component of thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine
Fluorine — incorporated into thyroid follicular cell membranes
Manganese — essential co-factor for thyroid peroxidase activity

questions.explanation: Iodine is a structural element of thyroid hormones T3 and T4; without it, the thyroid gland hypertrophies in a compensatory attempt to trap more iodine, producing endemic goitre. Selenium is the shrewdest wrong answer because it genuinely supports thyroid function via deiodinase enzymes — but selenium deficiency does not cause goitre; it exacerbates iodine deficiency and causes a distinct cardiomyopathy (Keshan disease).

questions.stem: A patient presents with angular cheilitis, a smooth magenta-coloured glossitis, and corneal vascularization. Which condition — termed 'ariboflavinosis' — accounts for this triad?

options.option_text: Vitamin B1 deficiency affecting peripheral nerve conduction
Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) deficiency disrupting mucosal integrity
Vitamin B6 deficiency causing seborrhoeic dermatitis features
Vitamin B9 deficiency impairing epithelial cell division rates

questions.explanation: Riboflavin (B2) is the precursor of FAD and FMN, co-enzymes critical for rapidly dividing mucosal cells; its deficiency causes the triad of angular cheilitis, magenta glossitis, and corneal vascularization, collectively called ariboflavinosis. B6 deficiency can produce a seborrhoeic-like rash but not corneal vascularization; B9 (folic acid) deficiency primarily causes megaloblastic anaemia with minimal mucosal signs.

questions.stem: In Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome, neuronal injury occurs because thiamine deficiency blocks a specific enzymatic step, causing toxic metabolite accumulation. Which biochemical event best explains the brain damage?

options.option_text: Ammonia clearance fails via impaired urea cycle in astrocytes
Pyruvate decarboxylation is blocked, causing lactate accumulation
Homocysteine remethylation fails due to impaired methionine synthase
Propionyl-CoA conversion fails, raising methylmalonic acid levels

questions.explanation: Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) is the co-factor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase; deficiency blocks entry of pyruvate into the TCA cycle, causing lactic acidosis and energy failure in the highly metabolically active mammillary bodies and thalamus. Option C (elevated homocysteine) mimics B12/folate deficiency; option D (methylmalonic acid rise) is specific to B12 deficiency — both are precision exam traps that exploit similar B-vitamin neurological presentations.

questions.stem: Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding in neonates occurs because certain coagulation factors require vitamin K–dependent gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues for calcium-binding activation. Which set of factors is rendered dysfunctional?

options.option_text: Factors I, V, VIII, and XIII — the fibrin cross-linking pathway
Factors II, VII, IX, and X — the vitamin K–dependent clotting factors
Factors VIII, IX, XI, and XII — the intrinsic tenase complex only
Factors III, XI, and von Willebrand factor — the extrinsic pathway

questions.explanation: Vitamin K acts as a co-factor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which carboxylates factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX, and X — as well as anticoagulant proteins C and S. Without carboxylation, these factors cannot bind calcium ions and remain biologically inert. Option C is the key trap: while haemophilia B involves factor IX, haemophilia is a genetic disorder; factors I, V, and VIII are not vitamin K–dependent and are unaffected in VKDB.
